_comment: Atlas's last stand (D191, replacing D73's tour; cut from 14 steps to 7 by D300): a new player's first game. It is the last day of Atlas's own world, in Hearthwick (data/areas/tutorial.json), run by src/ui/tutorial_guide.gd: the game's ways taught one step at a time, then a fight Atlas cannot win. He falls for good: he is written into the record of the fallen (src/chronicle/sixteen.gd) and his world is the first that ended, so the next lead is picked by the quiz, the opening shows his world going dark, his ghost sits at the fire and his weapon falls into the next world. Each step is done when its `done` happens: `did` (what EventBus.player_did says; a value ending in ':' or '_' matches any name), `flag` (set in GameState), `opened` ('party' or 'journal'), or `button`. A step may have `on_start` → `set_flag` (a list), set as it comes up: the fight steps call out the village's bands (`bands` in its area, D75). The step with `doom` is the last: when its fight ends, `fall` is shown and Atlas is written down. Nothing else here is saved.

steps.title: The last day of Atlas's world
steps.text:
You are Atlas, one of the sixteen, in the world that is his. Nothing you do in Hearthwick is saved. What happens to Atlas is.

Move with WASD or the arrow keys, or click the ground to walk there. Your company follows the leader. The line along the bottom always says what you can do where you stand.

steps.title: Talking
steps.text: Anyone with a ! over them has something to say. Walk up to Maren the Guide, by the signpost, and click her (or stand close and press E). Then ask her something: what the gates are, what the Tower is, what happens when someone falls.

steps.title: Buying
steps.text:
Pim keeps the stall. Ask what he's selling and buy something: food and draughts heal between fights, and gear makes your people stronger.

Not everyone will talk: Smudge, the fox in the hat, wants a coin, a good roll or a reason.

steps.title: Doing a favour
steps.text:
People ask for help. Ask Wren if she needs a hand, find what she lost (things worth a look are marked ?), then go back and tell her.

Walk onto a chest to open it, and into a door to go inside.

steps.title: Your company
steps.text: Press P for the party screen: everyone's health, gear and abilities, and where you choose a class when someone is ready to grow. N opens the journal: every creature you've met and the story of your run. Esc closes either.

steps.title: A sparring fight
steps.text:
Captain Harrow's sparring pair are out in the field south of the square now. The red cells are what they can see. Step into the red and the fight is on at once, right there on this ground. Out of their sight, press G to wind up a first strike: it lands before they turn. Long grass hides you, and bursting out of it at them is an ambush.

Space pauses and unpauses. Left-click or drag a box to pick fighters; right-click to move or attack. Q W E R use skills. Nobody can die in practice.

steps.title: The gate in the hills breaks
steps.text:
Every world of the sixteen is like this one: a land to walk, villages and keeps, the Guild's paid contracts, the Tower over everything, and the gates, where monsters pour out. Shut a gate by fighting through it; leave one open too long and it breaks.

One has broken. What was behind it is coming down the road into Hearthwick, its red ground ahead of it. Atlas cannot beat it. Fight it anyway: step into the red. In Earth Kings a fall is for good: when your lead dies, their world ends with them.

lines: Atlas falls in Hearthwick, and does not get up.
With him goes his world: the village, the road, the Tower over it, all of it going dark.
That is how it is for the sixteen. One life, one world. When a lead dies, their world ends, and the next of them begins again in another, knowing only what you learned.

skip.title: Atlas's last stand
skip.text: A new game begins with Atlas's last stand. Play it, or skip it? Skipped, he still falls: the run begins with the next of the sixteen.
